title: Composer Lanes — personal scratchpad
content:
Elevator: small personal brainstorm for a composable prompt-authoring surface that exposes lightweight policy lanes ("Composer Lanes") so product teams and power users can assemble modular prompt blocks and automatically apply fidelity/cost policies per-lane. Goal is a fast way to trade tokens vs. quality per block in a single turn and ship a usable MVP for the Console and SDKs.

Problem we see:
- Users assemble long prompts (context + instructions + examples) and can't easily tell which parts drive token cost vs. downstream quality.
- Engineers want predictable unit economics at the block level (e.g., allow high-fidelity safety checks but cheaper answer draft).
- Current UX forces global fidelity or per-request hacks (two calls, manual splitting) — painful for iterative product teams.

Core idea:
- Prompt is modeled as ordered blocks (lane: instruction, lane: evidence, lane: exemplar, lane: post-process). Each lane has a small profile: cost-preference (cheap/normal/high), max_tokens_hint, and execution policy (inline, background, tool-call).
- At generation, the runtime compiles lane profiles into either: single-call with internal steering, or multi-call plan (cheap seed -> refine in high lane). Redwood runtime will pick plan based on SLO and customer config (hosted vs. dedicated).

Concrete user stories:
- As a PM, I can drag an "explainability" block into my prompt and mark it "cheap" so answers keep high-level reasoning without exploding tokens.
- As an ML engineer, I can set default lane profiles for a product route so that new prompts inherit sensible cost/quality tradeoffs.
- As a developer, I can preview estimated tokens and an estimated p95 latency per lane before sending.

Success metrics (first 6 weeks):
- Adoption: 15 internal teams test Composer Lanes (Console + SDK) with at least 50 prompts created.
- Cost impact: 10% reduction in per-turn median tokens for routes that opt-in.
- Quality regressions: automated eval score drop <= 3% on primary datasets.

MVP scope (Console + Hosted API):
- Console: lane editor UI (add/rename/reorder lanes), per-lane cost-preference selector, token estimate.
- SDK: lane-presets as JSON envelope + server-side planner header => new API param: lane_profiles (backwards compatible).
- Runtime: simple compiler that can convert lane_profiles into either a single-call prompt with inline markers, or a two-stage call (draft -> refine).

Experiment matrix:
- Mode A: Inline single-call with system tags. Baseline latency, simpler UX, weaker cost wins.
- Mode B: Two-call staged generation (seed + refine). Higher latency, better cost savings.
- Mode C: Background cheap lane (async), best-effort enrich when capacity exists.

Telemetry & signals to collect:
- Per-lane token consumption, per-lane time to first byte, plan chosen (inline vs staged), number of fallbacks, cost delta vs historical baseline.
- User toggles: how often users pick "cheap" vs "high" for the same lane name.

Acceptance criteria (engineering):
- New lane_profiles header accepted by hosted API and validated.
- Console lane editor saves presets to user namespace and emits telemetry.
- Planner chooses inline vs staged heuristics based on sequence length and configured latency SLO.

Open questions / risks:
- How to present fidelity tradeoffs without confusing non-technical users? (need simple defaults + hover tips).
- Risk of hallucination increase if cheap lanes remove crucial context — require evals and guardrails.
- Billing / metering: do we show per-lane line-items in invoices? (privacy/billing complexity).
- Edge case: tool-calling lanes that must run synchronously. Planner complexity increases.

Rollout plan (quick):
1) Internal dogfood: product + solutions engineering try Console-only flow for 2 weeks.
2) Beta release: opt-in flag for orgs; enable telemetry and safety eval gating.
3) Iterate: add SDK ergonomics and examples, surface per-route presets in Optimize.

Notes / To-do:
- Sketch UI: left column lane list, middle lane canvas (markdown-ish blocks), right column cost preview + toggles.
- Prototype a lane_profiles JSON shape and backward-compatible header name (x-rw-lane-profiles).
- Sync with runtime team: what heuristics exist today for staged calls? Reuse warmup heuristics + KV cache.

Quick prototype tasks (next 10 days):
- Draft lane_profiles schema (Rowan)
- Console mock (Mira)
- Runtime plan prototype for Mode B (Ethan)
- Eval harness: two datasets to check hallucination/quality (Talia)

If this gets traction, follow-ups: lane marketplace (community-shared presets), lane-level eval traces, and per-lane micro-budgets on Dedicated.

Random brainstorming crumbs:
- "lane transforms": small post-processors attached to lanes (e.g., truncate, paraphrase, sanitize).
- quick toggle to run lane as a tool call (for expensive safety check).
- lane-level explainability: show which lane contributed most to the final tokens via token heatmap.

End of page (rough).
